title: Remedy Market: curated microfix recipe catalog with permissioned dry-run and circuit-breaker guard
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Problem: Oncall engineers repeatedly re-author ad-hoc one-off patches for common platform incidents (OOM, stuck tasklets, runaway queues). These fixes are fragile and lack uniform telemetry, RBAC, or safe rollback. Goal: build a permissioned "Remedy Market" — a curated catalog of small, typed remediation recipes (microfixes) that can be executed as runbook tasks from the Console or CLI, with sandboxable dry-run, automatic circuit-breaker gating, and telemetry/approval hooks.

Scope:
- A storage-backed catalog (metadata + typed inputs + semantic tags) surfaced via Console and internal API.
- A CLI "remedy" command to search and invoke recipes with typed validation and --dry-run.
- Execution runtime adapters for: server-side safe-executor (k8s job short-lived), opslet agent (ephemeral sidecar), and a mock simulator for dry-runs.
- Permission model: recipe owners + role-based approval flows; elevated recipes require multi-approver or PR-backed execution.
- Safety: pre-check validators, canary rollout (targeted hosts), timeboxed execution, automatic rollback where supported, and a circuit-breaker that halts a recipe if error rate or latency regressions exceed thresholds.
- Observability: structured telemetry events, per-invocation logs, performance metrics, and a Remedy Dashboard (filter by recipe, user, team, outcome).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Create/Update/Delete API for recipes with schema validation and markdown description.
2) Console UI to browse, preview typed input schema, and request approval.
3) CLI that supports search, dry-run, and execute; returns structured JSON output and links to invocation logs.
4) Execution path supports a safe-executor with timeouts and verification hooks; failing recipes automatically open a remediation ticket.
5) Circuit-breaker and telemetry emit events to the existing ops-telemetry pipeline; runbook-level SLO impact visible on Console.

Non-goals: full public marketplace, third-party recipe uploading, or general-purpose scripting engine. We will only support vetted, reviewed recipes initially.

Implementation notes / trade-offs:
- Catalog storage: use existing runbook service DB namespace (avoid adding another datastore). Pros: reuse permissions and audit trails. Cons: tighter coupling to runbook data model; ensure migration compatibility.
- Execution: prefer short-lived k8s jobs in Dedicated clusters for isolation; fallback to opslet for edge cases (on-prem). This increases infra complexity but gives clearer isolation.
- Dry-run fidelity: simulator will run validations and dry-path but cannot fully replicate stateful rollbacks; documentation must highlight simulator limitations.

Security and compliance: integrate with RBAC and audit logs; require KMS-signed approvals for high-privilege recipes. Security review is required prior to release (see security_review_required).

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Remedy+Market+PRD
- Design mockups (Console): https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/remedy-market-v1.png
- Prototype CLI: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-tools/pull/879
- Telemetry dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops/remedy-invocations-staging

Rollout plan: begin with internal beta (SRE + Support) for 2 weeks, collect telemetry and refine pre-checks, then expand to platform engineers, finally enable team-level browse for all orgs with opt-in approvals.

Risks: accidental privilege escalation via poorly written recipes, false sense of dry-run safety, and operational churn from recipe maintenance. Mitigations include mandatory owner review, automatic test harness for each recipe, and quarterly catalog pruning.
